newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Discovery plans Australia gas search.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Discovery plans Australia gas search.

text.p: Exploration work is planned to find more gas near the Beharra Springs gasfields project in Western Australia, 33 percent owned by Discovery Petroleum NL, a Discovery official told Reuters on Thursday.

A new gas well would enable the project to extend the life of an existing gas processing plant at Beharra Springs after three wells operated by 67 percent owner Boral Ltd dry up by around 2005, John Begg, Discovery's development manager said.
Beharra Springs is located in EP320 permit, in the Perth Basin.
Discovery is currently the target of a takeover bid by the Australian arm of Premier Oil Plc of Britain.
Discovery earlier on Thursday advised shareholders to take no immediate action on Premier's latest offer of A$0.80 a share.
The latest offer is 10 cents higher than Premier's earlier offer of A$0.70 a share.
Discovery ended trading on Thursday at A$0.80.
"We've told shareholders to take a wait and see position," Begg said.

He said Discovery's largest shareholder, Oil Search Ltd, which recently paid A$0.75 share for a 10.1 percent stake in Discovery, and has been cited as a possible second suitor by analysts, was reviewing Premier's latest bid.
Premier has denied claims by analysts that it is less interested in Discovery's Australian assets than it is in its Indonesian holdings in the Kakap region, near some of its own properties.
Begg said a new discovery near Beharra Springs could extend the life of the project, which to date has produced 82,000 barrels of condensate and 33.8 petajoules of gas.

Discovery also is nearing an agreement with a farm-in partner to fund exploration of its 87 percent-owned Sundalara gas project in the northern Perth Basin in return for up to 50 percent stakes in Discovery's Perth Basin interests, excluding Beharra Springs, Begg said.
